text:
sarah: Heads-up — CI perf smoke failed on canary in eu-west-1 (H100 pool). 95p token latency jumped ~4x, blocking the rollout. holding rollout.
raj: which perf job? link: https://ci.redwood/teams/infra/jobs/ci-perf/1123
sarah: job ci-perf/llm-infer-1024. baseline 95p ~220ms, canary 95p ~950ms, p99 4.2s. Only repros on H100 nodes in eu-west-1. A10/L4 pools unaffected.
mike: quick grep of runtime logs during the job shows kernel_selector picked `warp_gelu_matmul_v2` on H100 after commit a2b7f3. Prior to that we used `fused_gelu_matmul_v1` for these shapes.
lexi: also noticed KV cache hit rate drop on the same runs: baseline hit_rate 87% -> canary 54%. That alone can explain spike in tail latency.
raj: interesting — could be kernel swap changed memory layout or batch pacing that increases KV churn. any flame/profile snippets?
mike: pasting small perf extract:
```
THREAD: runtime_worker_7  cpu=H100-0
cpu_cycles: 1.2e9
matmul_kernel (warp_gelu_v2): 42.1%
kv_lookup: 18.4% (miss cost high)
mem_copies: 12.7%
wait_io: 8.9%
```
vs baseline:
```
matmul_kernel (fused_gelu_v1): 35.0%
kv_lookup: 9.2%
mem_copies: 9.0%
wait_io: 6.0%
```
lexi: big delta on kv_lookup — miss cost doubled. suspect changed batching/padding behavior causing more unique prefixes so cache keys bloom. PR a2b7f3 also nudged the continuous batching heuristic to prefer lower padding for throughput.
raj: i started a targeted bisect locally. quick note: network retransmits on the eu-west H100 NICs are also slightly up during canary windows (eth0 rx_errors+retries up 0.7%). could be noisy neighbor + kernel change amplifying tail.
infra-bot: canary deployment triggered: canary/eu-west-1/h100-pool @ 2026-02-28T14:03:10Z (id: canary-789)
lexi: running a controlled repro forcing old kernel: set ENV RUNTIME_KERNEL_FORCE=fused_gelu_v1 and batching_pacer=legacy.
mike: local repro with env override restores baseline: 95p back to ~240ms, KV hit rate 85%. So kernel_selector change appears causal.
raj: but we should be careful: batching heuristic tweak might be contributing. Hard to separate fully without isolating both changes.
sarah: plan: 1) run canary with only kernel selector reverted, keep batching change; 2) run canary with only batching reverted, keep kernel change; 3) if kernel-only revert fixes, rollback that commit and block merge.
lexi: running job 1184 with kernel-only revert in eu-west H100 now. command: `./deploy/canary --pool h100 --patch revert:a2b7f3:kernel-selector`
sarah: also opened a perf CI job to run a quick KV-cache smoke on every PR touching kernel/batching: https://ci.redwood/pipeline/perf-smoke
mike: output from partial run (kernel-only revert) after 12 minutes:
```
95p: 260ms
99p: 730ms
KV_hit_rate: 84.6%
net_retransmits: baseline+0.2%
```
lexi: that's convincing. kernel change increases KV miss cost on H100.
raj: created bisect note: suspect PR #4129 (runtime: smarter kernel selector) — it enabled warp_gelu_v2 for H100 shapes. mike, can you draft revert MR for just that subchange?
mike: drafted MR: https://git.redwood/reverts/mr-813 — revert kernel selector lines only. tagging @sarah @oncall.
sarah: created rollback MR 1763490456, marking rollout-blocker. Hold all releases touching runtime kernel selector until postmortem.
deploy-bot: Revert MR merged to canary branch at 2026-02-28T14:12:34Z, starting canary redeploy.
infra-bot: canary redeploy healthy in eu-west-1/h100-pool — metrics back within 10% of baseline after 8m.
lexi: follow-ups: add regression test that runs small seq=512+seq=1024 traces on H100 pool for both kernel paths; add kv-hit_rate dashboard by pool/model/kernel combo; instrument kernel_selector to record decision + reason to help future triage.
raj: also add network quasi-noise monitor (NIC retransmits) to canary health so we don't miss noisy neighbor amplification.
sarah: agreed. Opening tickets: PERF-226 (H100 kernel perf test), OBS-88 (kv hit-rate per kernel), INFRA-411 (NIC retransmit monitor).
mike: note for postmortem: kernel_selector heuristics were tuned on host with different seq distribution (shorter tails), missed H100 memory-path subtlety — need platform-specific microbenchmarks.
lexi: thanks everyone. big win to catch in canary before wide rollout. :thumbsup:
sarah: pinging @oncall to do short postmortem and inform product about rollback.
raj: will add short incident timeline in #incidents later.
